column4: The section contrasts two named springs by what their water does; 2:60 describes Moses striking a rock so twelve springs gush out and each group knows where to drink, a concrete communal spring scene.
The section treats the flowing spring as provision; 7:160 repeats the spring-gushing scene and explicitly tells the people to eat and drink from God's provision.

The section stresses that springs share a name while their qualities differ; 13:4 says gardens are watered by one water yet differ in their produce, a specific parallel between common source and unlike outcomes.
The section places moving water in a garden; 18:33 describes two gardens through which a river runs, a concrete garden-and-flowing-water parallel.
The section joins water to food as provision; 23:19 continues the account of water settled in the earth in 23:18 by describing gardens, abundant fruit, and eating from it.
The section's garden has a flowing spring; 36:34 says God made gardens and caused springs to gush in them, a direct garden-and-spring scene.
The section treats drinking and food as one provision; 36:35 completes the garden-and-spring scene of 36:34 by saying people may eat from its fruit.
The section contrasts moving spring water with water that may sink away; 39:21 describes rain made into springs in the earth, then plants drying and crumbling, showing the source's renewal and loss.
The section links garden springs with nourishment; 55:67 continues the pair of gushing springs in 55:66 by naming the date palms and pomegranates of those gardens.
The section says placed cups are the opposite of raised furnishings; 56:34 describes raised couches in the garden scene whose preceding verses mention poured water and enduring fruit.
The section makes the hot spring a punishment drink; 56:42 places the condemned in scorching wind and boiling water, repeating the punitive heat-and-water pairing.
The section opposes the hot spring to refreshing garden water; 56:44 says the punishment's shade is neither cool nor beneficial, clarifying that no relief comes from the scene.
The section sets garden drink against punitive food and water; 37:62 asks whether the garden's welcome or the tree of Zaqqum is the better provision, introducing the contrast that 37:66–67 completes.
